title: Uptown versus downtown bands and Bob Lyons's band
summary: Uptown bands faked more, downtown was more musically trained; he describes Bob Lyons's band, its jobs and personnel.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I don't know. I don't remember Dave Ogden being with the Maple Leaf Band. I wanted to ask about if you noticed any difference in the bands uptown and the ones downtown. Like Bob Lyons, did they play a different type of music or a different beat or anything in your Maple Leaf? Same type. No, same type. Because they had this fellow, Wesley Dine from Baton Rouge, he was dead. He was playing trumpet. Most of all the fellas were playing around here. And they all were playing about this thing. They weren't any rougher uptown then than down? No, no, no. Or they did more faking uptown or anything? Some people say. Oh, they did more faking uptown. Your better class of resistance was always from downtown. They did more faking up there more than that. That's what I thought. Some people told me that I wondered if that was true. Yeah, that's the truth. That's the truth, Dad. The Cortmota, people on this side. You see, a long time ago, the kind of type of music when you get in those orchestras. They would play plenty of brothers who couldn't play. We used to have what they called shouts, mazooka, apulka, and things like that. And lots of bands that couldn't play that. Take an orchestra to play that. And if you was not a drummer that read, you couldn't make it. But outside of that, they played the same kind of type of music as Dixie Lamb music. And it was very sudden that you'd catch a fellow from the band from uptown with a high fellow on this side of Canal Street. And most of them would take the click that he got up there. And we used to stick on this side. Did Bob Lyons like your drumming and had you then? Oh yeah, I don't care who was playing the drum with Bob Lyons. I went up there and said, Bob, I might work. Come on and work. The Maple Leaf Band was the same way. I don't care who was there. I got that. You know, I wanted to. Do you remember any of the other uptown bands like Frankie Duesen? What kind of a band did he have? Do you remember? Well, I remember Frankie Duesen. I remember Kid Punch too. Well, they had most of this, you know, play anything, anywhere. When you played with Bob Lyons, what kind of jobs did he have? Were they dances or fraternity dates or what kind of? Yeah, plenty of fraternity dates. Yeah, people were crazy about it. Yeah, plenty of fraternity dates. Plenty of fraternity.

I know Bob was on bass. Little Wesley Dime. First they had Ricard playing trumpet. You know Ricard? He died the other day. But he was playing trumpet. And after Ricard left, then they had this fellow Diane from Baton Rouge. They had a fellow by the name of Freddie Booboo who was playing trombone. And they had a Lorenzo Starr on guitar. On bandle at least. On guitar, bandle. And it had Bob Lyons on bass.
Did you ever have Fess with you? Fess?

With Bob Lyons. When Fess told us he played some dates like we did. Yeah, Fess played dates with Bob too. At the same time as you did? Yeah, yeah, yeah. He played piano then? Played piano. Yeah, played piano. Yeah, Fess did.

Was it Bob that used to act up a little bit with the bass? Think how he was riding it? Sort of act up a little bit on the stage with it? He put on a little act to resolve it with it? Have you ever seen him do that? Bob? Well, not to my point.

I mean, you know, like all bass players. Some people told us he used to swing it around, you know, a good deal. Maybe get out in the middle of the floor and sort of ride it and things like that too. Yeah, yeah, yeah, they'd swing about like that. But I mean, that's natural. Yeah. That's what most of the bass players does, you know. He was a nice fella.
Did you ever work with Ernest Kelly?
Ernest Kelly played trombone with Bob too. Bob used to change the musician sometimes. I could change Shirley. What about Shelley Du Congdre?
Probably Du Congdre. That's how they do Congdre. That's how they do Congdre. Thank you.
